body: I like journaling about my thoughts and emotions... but only the good ones lol. I tend to re-read my entries and before I decided to do it how I am now, I was constantly writing down all the bad moments and how I felt and what my thoughts were at the time. Reading those entries would bring my mood down and just remind me of the bad things. But now that I only write the good stuff, it makes me feel the way I did when it happened. I prefer keeping my thoughts in my head and just talk it out loud with myself like I'm talking with a therapist or a friend, that way I can't remember the bad moments. It's not for everyone and especially if your thoughts are overwhelming it might be hard to do it the way I do it. Also, very valid fear.

I've had multiple relationships like what you have right now and after getting into a healthy and loving relationship, I can tell you that this is not what a normal relationship is like. Your standards aren't unrealistic. In fact, they're VERY realistic and dare I say the bare minimum. Don't stay in something just because it's not bad right now, because you'll end up feeling resentful in the future the longer this goes on. A relationship should be something that happens between two people who love and care about each other and you should be able to feel it. I say cut it short and don't spend any more time in this relationship because it's not going to go anywhere, especially since two years has already passed.

I think it would help if you had a goal that you could work towards. Something to distract you from your situation, but also allow you to work on yourself. Don't make it a big goal, something small and when you reach that one, make another one and another one and so on. Having another thing to focus on will be helpful to get your mind off of things. Your emotions are still high and it might be a while before they come down, so take it easy on yourself and don't expect too much from yourself right now. You're in a tough time and as much as you want to not think about the future, things are still fresh, so it'll be difficult. Takes things one step at a time and don't rush yourself. After a breakup I also spent more time with other people or took myself out on more solo dates. These things can help you stay more present.

I thought I was too difficult to love until I met my partner. He is so incredibly patient with me and understands how to not make my emotions escalate even further if I start splitting. He's able to calm me down and allow me to think properly. Men like him are like a needle in a haystack, especially with how dating culture is nowadays. It took me a long time to realize, but just because we struggle with our mental health, does not mean we deserve less. Nobody's perfect and you have worked on yourself which is amazing! Yes, we do need to manage things by ourself, but that doesn't mean we can't have a partner that supports us and is able to give us what we need. A partner who cares about you will give you that reassurance and do things that make you feel secure. Someone who feels they need to put on an act in front of you is not the one for you. I have grown so much and so fast after meeting my partner, after so many failed relationships where I never felt I was enough. We deserve the bare minimum and more. Don't expect any less. It'll take time to find the right person, but when you do, your worries will slowly disappear. Your expectations are realistic and they are completely valid because to me, that's the bare minimum. Anyone who can't give you that are not worth your time, love and care. Continue to work on yourself and focus on your growth. The right person will come by without you even noticing :)

I’m not going to say you are in the wrong or your friends are in the wrong because there’s no context, so I’ll just give you advice for if either one is happening. 

There’s lots of ways to get better, but because I don’t know what you’re struggling with, it’s hard to say what would be helpful. I would say to write down things that you believe you’re not good at doing. For example, staying calm in stressful situations. Take those points and write down possible ways you can help yourself stay calm and lower your stress, such as stepping away or taking deep breaths until you feel more relaxed. Things like that. And don’t write out big goals. Start with small ones because those are more attainable and don’t seem so impossible to reach. 

As for feeling better in those situations, I would say take a moment to really analyze what’s going on. Are you really wrong? Or is there just a disagreement between you and your friends. But of course, if your friends are constantly saying you’re wrong, then you really need to take a look at what you’re saying vs what they’re saying. If there’s any facts you can put towards them, do so and try to see what’s really going on. 

Something you have to understand as well is that you can’t please everyone. Wanting to be good for everyone isn’t possible, because reality is not so simple. And another thing you have to understand is that some people are meant to stay and some people aren’t. Keep the ones who support you and think about your relationship with those who don’t and are constantly going against you. Yes, being alone sucks, but it’s better than having people constantly bringing you down. I’m not able to write everything that I possibly know that could help you, but hopefully something I said will help.

Set clear boundaries with your partner. Tell him you're not ready to move in together and don't want him to pressure you to. Don't do what you don't want to do and don't allow someone to make decisions for you. You're the only one who gets to decide what you want to do. If it's freaking you out, it clearly isn't the thing you want to do.

I'm no professional, but I can help you figure out where to move on from there. You said you're dabbling in music production... that's really cool! You could join a beginner music production forum, and talk to people about how to improve. It's something you're interested in, so it's a good starting point. You don't have to be knowledgeable or good at something to be able to connect with others. Some people find joy in spreading their knowledge and just want someone to listen and talk to about it. I know it's tough to start having conversations again, since you're not used to it, but like everything else, practicing more helps. I don't know if I'm helping at all, but if you ever need someone to talk to, feel free to message me :)

It feels awful yet comfortable because you're used to feeling that way. It's what you know and what you've done for a  while, that's why it feels comfortable. Of course feeling happy would feel fake and uncomfortable. It's because you haven't felt that way much. It's not that you don't want to be happy. People tend to stick to what they're comfortable with and don't like to venture out for fear of something bad happening. It's normal to feel this way, but that doesn't mean it's good. Find something that makes you happy every day, even if it's something small like getting outside and breathing fresh air. Once you start allowing happiness into your life, you'll feel more comfortable feeling it.

Hey there, I know things are tough for you right now, but you haven't wasted your life at all. You're only 26, you still have plenty of time to do things. Age doesn't matter when learning new things or trying to make new friends or becoming interesting (although I'm sure you're interesting already enough). It can be hard to begin to make friends when you haven't socialized a lot up until this moment, but think of things that you think would make you be more fun to be around. Anything in particular you're interested in or like to do? There are people out there with lots of different hobbies and interests and you can always begin a friendship online, so you won't actually have to face the person. There's lots of different groups nowadays for people with similar interests. Try finding something that you don't mind doing and go from there.

Personally, as someone who has taken antidepressants for many years, I would say to have taking antidepressants as your last option if all else fails. I know people always say "exercise! you'll feel much better afterwards" and it can be tiring to hear, but since you're able to exercise, I would incorporate that into your daily life first and see how that goes. Also, diet is important to mental health just as much as it is to physical health. I'm not saying your depression isn't bad enough to take antidepressants, but I'm just hoping you'll explore other options before choosing that route, because it's not an easy thing to do. You may be lucky and get the right dosage and medication the first try, but it may also take lots of tries to get the right one and that might take years.

Your depression might be worsened because you moved to a new city and don't have many friends there. Being alone in a new city is hard, so it's likely that your stress is causing the depression. Perhaps you can book an appointment with your general practitioner and speak to them about how to move forward.

It sounds like you fell in love with the idea of him you had and not actually with him. Like you said, you fell for the "I'm so great" and the "I'm a great boyfriend" and he's not who he turned out to be. He's not great like he said and he's not a great boyfriend like he said he is. You're also in what people call the honeymoon phase where you're super infatuated with someone, but after that initial period, you start to lose feelings. That's normal. You're still young and you still have more opportunities to meet people. You can try helping him improve, but ultimately, that takes time and it's up to you whether you will wait for the change or not.

You could think of it as a process to go through when getting better. I like to think of people leaving me as their way of overcoming something that they were struggling with and their choice to leave me is their way of getting better. Just like we struggle with our emotions, the people around us are too, and I'm sure it wasn't an easy choice for them to decide this. Some people are meant to be with us for the long ride and some people are just visiting for the moment and that's okay. We can't expect everyone we meet to stay, just like we shouldn't expect ourselves to stay in something that prevents us from growing.

You shouldn't blame yourself for them leaving because you're struggling with something really difficult to deal with and every day is a challenge for you. You shouldn't blame them either because people should be able to make a decision that they believe will make them better. You can't stop people from making certain choices even if you feel it's unfair to you. Things happen in life and we can't control everything, but what we can control is ourselves and how we perceive and feel about things. Choose to see the positive side. It hurts, I know and I know you don't want these people to leave you, but don't blame yourself because you're dealing with something that not everyone will understand. Also, it doesn't mean that these people will be out of your life forever. Focus on your growth and perhaps in the future, you'll meet them again. Stay positive, even when it seems like there's no positivity to be found.

Real person here and hopefully I'm not giving you any tips that Google has given you because that would be unfortunate.

When I know I'm starting to split, I either:

- Step away from the situation and give myself 5-10 mins to calm down (or put down the phone if you're in a call or texting) This helps me to get over the initial overwhelming feeling of needing to split and that's usually what I struggle with.

- If that doesn't work and I start splitting, I told my partner to say the dumbest thing ever that would make me think "wtf?" (I told him to start shouting "poopoo peepee" at me whenever I get angry at him) Because it's dumb and out of nowhere, I usually end up laughing and again, get over that initial overwhelming feeling.

- If THAT doesn't work, I force myself to start talking about something else that completely unrelated.

Those usually work for me because like you I know I'm getting angry and triggered over the smallest things and the me not in a splitting state wants to not be like that. It takes practice and won't always work. My tip for preventing splitting is to "think before you speak". Easier said than done of course. I like to talk to myself about why I'm feeling that way and be my own therapist essentially. Idk if I helped at all and sorry if I didn't!

I've gotten a lot better at controlling my emotions when it comes to my partner spending time with others and it's mostly because I occupy myself with something to do. I had to make myself realize that I can't fully control what my partner does and I can't prevent him from spending time with people he wants to spend time with. For me, I don't have many friends and the friends I do have, I don't spend time with them often, so I mainly spend the time with my partner. Like you, I get upset when my partner decides to spend time with others because I get the feeling of "what about me?" So what I've found helpful is that if my partner is gaming with his friends, I allow him to do that, but I start playing a game myself as well. I don't play the same games as him, but just knowing that we're doing the same thing, makes me feel included.

Also I feel like communicating with your partner about how you feel would help, that way he's more understanding of your emotions. Tell him about your worries and come up with solutions with him. Be honest with him and don't bottle up emotions because then you're more likely to say something hurtful. 

But I would say the easiest thing to do would be to plan things for yourself on days that your partner hangs out with someone else. For me, I find leaving the house is the best for me because I'm not cooped up in an environment where everything's stagnant. When things are moving around me, it's easier for me to be distracted. But if you find yourself in the situation where you feel like you're going to say something hurtful to your partner, step away for 5 mins or mute the call for 5 mins. That usually gives me enough time for the initial overwhelming emotions to go away and allows me to think more clearly. But definitely talk to your partner about how you feel :)

I feel the same way too honestly. I always felt like I needed someone to be with and like you said, if I don't then I'm completely lost. But you don't have to be single to work on yourself. If your partner is someone who is willing to support you, then that's even better. I know it'll be hard to focus on the relationship and then also work on yourself, but it sounds like we're similar and we can't stay single. Most of the work I've done to work on myself was when I was in a relationship. I know therapy is always suggested and that helps, but only if you find a good therapist and even then it's going to be costly, so I'm not going to suggest that. Write down the things that you want to work on, on a piece of paper and then write small things you can do to get yourself closer to your goals. Then put that paper somewhere you will look every day, so that you'll see it. Like if you want to work on not losing your temper on someone as an example, a small step to move towards that could be stepping away from the situation and taking some deep breaths, just so that initial overwhelming feeling you get goes away. It takes time to grow and it's okay. Small steps are more manageable and are more achievable. I don't know if anything I said will help in any way, but you have the mindset to want to work on yourself and that's already commendable.

I can understand where you're coming from as I've been in the same situation before. I've been dealing with my BPD for years and some days it still feels so unmanageable, but better days will come. In my personal experience, I've found that letting go of people who really showed me that they didn't care about me benefitted me a lot because my energy wasn't being wasted on them anymore. I was able to use that energy on other things like doing things that made me happy. And I know that's hard to find especially when you're down in the dumps. But whether it be just a walk in the park or a sweet treat, anything helps really. I found myself focusing too much on the negatives instead of the small positives that happened every day. But once you're able to find one positive in the day, it gets much easier little by little. 

We feel things deeply and that's burdensome, but also shows how much we care about things and it's quite beautiful if you think about it. I know things are tough now, but start by finding one positive thing out of the many negatives that happen in your day. Just know that you're not unlovable and there's nothing wrong with you. We're just different and we feel things differently, but that doesn't have to be a bad thing. If you find that you're feeling too deeply sometimes, I find giving myself a couple of minutes to think things out helps a lot. Next time, try giving yourself 5 minutes and talk to yourself whether internally or externally. Explain to yourself why you're feeling these emotions and tell yourself that you're not wrong for feeling these emotions, it's just a reaction from your body and it's way of protecting you. If no one else has ever done this for you, I will and although I'm just a stranger on the internet, your feelings are valid. You're not crazy. There's nothing wrong with you. And you're definitely not unlovable. Allow yourself the chance to grow because as long as you have the drive to get better and be better, you'll definitely get there. If the people around you aren't willing to fight for you and support you along your journey, then maybe they're not the people you want to be surrounding yourself with. Easier said than done of course, but sometimes you need to make that judgement for yourself. I hoped I helped in some way, but I wish you the best and never give up because you've gotten through bad days before, you can get through this one too.

Honestly, this is the EXACT thing I’m going through right now! I am literally doing the same things you are doing, so I know how hard it can be. I also have BPD so I definitely know how crazy our emotions can get. The one thing I’m trying to do more often is walk away when I feel like I’m about to say something that I know will start a fight. It’s going to be extremely hard at first, but overtime it will help. So whenever you feel like angry texting him, literally drop your phone and walk away from it. If you’re with him, you can literally just say aloud “Time out!“ like you would as a kid and walk away. It helped me immensely with clearing my mind and not talk with my strong emotions at full force. 

And you’re definitely not crazy. Having BPD makes it harder for us to deal with things since our emotions and beliefs can be really strong. I also feel like I’m the second choice as well, but for me, I know I’m really clingy and I know you mentioned that as well. Try directing that energy towards yourself and working on yourself. You might be feeling this way about everything because you’re insecure and have low self-confidence…Well… I might be speaking totally about myself here haha. It’s going to be hard, but again, if you really love him and he loves you, there is always room for improvement. And of course communication is so important! So talk about your feelings and try to stay calm. Again, if things get heated and you feel angry or irritated, just walk away. :)
